Joke: Why did the radiologist keep calm during the code? He had a lot of exposure to stress.
Our autoclave has better attendance than half the internet. It shows up, it runs hot, it never calls out.
A patient asked if the procedure was minimally invasive. I said yes — the paperwork is the invasive part.
Turnover time is the only thing in this building that grows without anyone feeding it.
Medical fact: The genicular arteries were mapped in the 1800s, but embolizing them for knee OA only became routine in the last decade — GAE is younger than most of our equipment.
The saphenous vein is the longest vein in the body — roughly the length of your leg plus your thigh, which is why ablation planning matters so much.
Contrast-induced nephropathy risk drops meaningfully with simple pre-procedure hydration. The cheapest intervention in the suite is a glass of water.
A lead apron blocks about 90–95% of scatter at typical fluoro energies — but only where it actually covers you. Cracks are not cosmetic.
Science fact: Your blood vessels laid end to end would circle the Earth roughly 2.5 times.
Water is one of the very few substances that is less dense as a solid — which is why ice floats and why lakes freeze top-down.
The human body replaces about 330 billion cells every day. You are, functionally, a slow-motion rebuild.
Sound travels about 4 times faster in water than in air — which is the whole reason ultrasound gel exists.
Word of the day: Ischemia — reduced blood supply to tissue. From Greek ischein (to hold back) + haima (blood). Literally: held-back blood.
Tortuous — full of twists and turns. Not to be confused with torturous, which is what a tortuous vessel feels like at 4 PM.
Patent — open, unobstructed. In vascular work the best possible thing to say about a vessel.
Meticulous — showing great attention to detail. From Latin metus, fear. The original sense was "fearful" — which is honestly the right instinct in an OR.
Motivation: Nobody notices a smooth day. That is what a smooth day is — the absence of everything going wrong, because someone checked the cart.
The turnover you save is not paperwork. It is one more patient who gets treated this month.
Do the boring thing correctly and the exciting thing never has to happen.
